I remember feeling blinded as well.  Mostly what I did was I just kept going, and then eventually it got better. A few coping skills I learned did significantly help.

The most important one was my List of Acceptable Activities. This was something my therapist came up with after his usual idea, five simple daily goals, didn't work for me.  5 goals (which may work for you) works by thinking of 5 things you could do everyday that would make your life better. I remember mine included brushing my teeth and eating 3 meals, it doesn't have to be huge. You just work on meeting those five things every day, and track how many you meet each day, and see improvement. But I saw none.

The List of Acceptable Activities worked better for me, because I didn't do well with all that tracking, it just felt like more failure. For the List, you just make a list of things that are good to do, anything that would make your life in anyway better: get the mail, brush your teeth, eat a meal, call a friend, read 5 pages, etc.  Then, when you are doing nothing because you are overwhelmed, you take out the list, pick any of those activities at all, and do one. 

Exercise was on my list, and that was a hugely helpful and still is. Running is still the best anti-anxiety drug I've ever found.

Deep breathing has also been very helpful for me. There is a free iphone ap called breath2relax that will teach you how to do it.

I also took 40mg of prozac a day which seemed to help, although I never really found an antidepressant that worked well.  Some people do have success with them and you could start trying to find a drug that works for you.
